sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学促进所有生物生活质量的使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Julia Barton has been thinking about what happens when we build big.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅·巴顿一直在思考当我们进行大型建设时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Maybe because she grew up in Dallas in the go-go 80s.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为她在80年代那个蓬勃发展的时期在达拉斯长大。

sentences.en: Big football arenas, big freeways, big houses.
sentences.zh: 巨大的足球场、宽阔的高速公路、庞大的住宅。

sentences.en: Texans love big.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯人热爱宏大。

sentences.en: Dallas built a new city hall in 1978.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯在1978年建造了一座新的市政厅。

sentences.en: Designed by I.M.
sentences.zh: 由贝聿铭设计。

sentences.en: Pei.
sentences.zh: 贝。

sentences.en: It's this huge trapezoid jutting over a wide plaza.
sentences.zh: 它是一个巨大的梯形建筑，矗立在一个宽阔的广场之上。

sentences.en: It's kind of wedge-shaped, but upside down, so the widest and largest floor is on the top.
sentences.zh: 它有点像楔形，但却是倒过来的，所以最宽、最大的楼层在顶部。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, sometimes I'd go up to the top floor of city hall with my friends.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我有时会和朋友们一起去市政厅的顶层。

sentences.en: That's where the vending machines were.
sentences.zh: 那里有自动售货机。

sentences.en: They stocked my favorite candy bar, Caramello.
sentences.zh: 它们存放着我最喜欢的巧克力棒，Caramello。

sentences.en: Then we'd sit by the windows eating chocolate and looking down over the plaza,
sentences.zh: 然后我们会坐在窗边吃着巧克力，俯瞰着广场，

sentences.en: and I'd think, wow, this is so cool.
sentences.zh: 我会想，哇，这太酷了。

sentences.en: But later in high school, Julia went to a protest down below in the plaza.
sentences.zh: 但后来在高中时，朱莉娅去广场下参加了一次抗议活动。

sentences.en: And those same city hall windows were now hulking over us.
sentences.zh: 而那些同样的市政厅窗户现在正沉重地压在我们头顶上。

sentences.en: We could see our tiny reflections in the glass.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到自己在玻璃上微小的倒影。

sentences.en: It made me feel like a nobody, and that this whole event was a waste of time,
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得自己像个无名小卒，整个活动也只是在浪费时间，

sentences.en: and all of the big things in my environment seemed to be saying the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我周围所有巨大的事物似乎都在诉说着同样的事情。

sentences.en: I'm important.
sentences.zh: 我很重要。

sentences.en: You're nobody.
sentences.zh: 你什么都不是。

sentences.en: So Julia developed a mistrust of the big building, the big project,
sentences.zh: 于是朱莉娅对大型建筑、大型项目产生了不信任感，

sentences.en: and places where people seemed to love the glory of the grandiose.
sentences.zh: 也对那些人们似乎沉迷于宏大荣耀的地方产生了怀疑。

sentences.en: But I'm also fascinated by those kinds of places.
sentences.zh: 但我同时也对这类地方着迷。

sentences.en: I can't stay away from them.
sentences.zh: 我无法远离它们。

sentences.en: Case in point, Russia.
sentences.zh: 以俄罗斯为例。

sentences.en: Biggest country in the world makes Texans look like amateurs.
sentences.zh: 世界上国土面积最大的国家让德克萨斯人看起来都像业余选手。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The Russians are real pros in the department of tall, towering, and humongous.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在高耸、巍峨和庞大这一领域绝对是专家。

sentences.en: And not just from the Soviet paSt.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是从苏联时期开始。

sentences.en: Europe's tallest skyscraper, 93 stories, is going up right now in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 欧洲最高的摩天大楼，93层，目前正在莫斯科拔地而起。

sentences.en: Though they had to stop for a while on the 67th floor after it caught fire.
sentences.zh: 尽管在发生火灾后，他们在第67层不得不停工了一段时间。

sentences.en: Russia's southernmost city, Sochi, is the biggest construction site in Europe.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯最南端的城市索契，是欧洲最大的建筑工地。

sentences.en: That's because Sochi is hosting the Winter Olympics in 2014.
sentences.zh: 这是因为索契将举办2014年冬季奥运会。

sentences.en: So I headed down there to check it out.
sentences.zh: 所以我前往那里一探究竟。

sentences.en: I went on a two-hour bus ride from Sochi's center on the Black Sea
sentences.zh: 我从黑海边的索契市中心坐了两个小时的巴士，

sentences.en: up to the foothills of the Caucasus, where they're building the ski resorts.
sentences.zh: 前往高加索山麓，他们正在那里建造滑雪胜地。

sentences.en: And maybe on that whole ride, there were a couple of five-minute stretches
sentences.zh: 在整个行程中，可能只有几次五分钟的间隙，

sentences.en: where I wasn't looking at a crane or a new hotel or a bridge going up.
sentences.zh: 我没有看到起重机、新酒店或正在建设的桥梁。

sentences.en: I also met this man named Alexey Kravets.
sentences.zh: 我还遇到了一个叫阿列克谢·克拉维茨的人。

sentences.en: He's lived all his life in a cinder block house by the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 他一生都住在黑海边的一栋煤渣砖房里。

sentences.en: The city wants to tear it down for a new rail yard.
sentences.zh: 市政府想拆掉它来建一个新的铁路编组站。

sentences.en: They've already demolished the rest of his neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们已经拆毁了他社区的其他部分。

sentences.en: But Kravets has appealed his eviction in court.
sentences.zh: 但克拉维茨已经在法庭上对他的驱逐令提出了上诉。

sentences.en: He says construction workers come up every day
sentences.zh: 他说建筑工人每天都会过来，

sentences.en: to scrape his walls with backhoes to scare him.
sentences.zh: 用挖掘机刮擦他的墙壁来恐吓他。

sentences.en: We never ask the government for anything, is what Kravets is saying.
sentences.zh: 克拉维茨说，我们从不向政府索要任何东西。

sentences.en: And now the government wants to take everything away from us.
sentences.zh: 而现在政府却想夺走我们的一切。

sentences.en: He's painted slogans in red paint on his windows,
sentences.zh: 他在窗户上用红漆写下了标语，

sentences.en: things like, people live here and SOS.
sentences.zh: 比如“这里有人居住”和“SOS”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sometimes construction workers throw rocks through the windows.
sentences.zh: 有时建筑工人会往窗户里扔石头。

sentences.en: They fall in shards of Cyrillic all over the floor.
sentences.zh: 它们化作西里尔字母的碎片散落在地板上。

sentences.en: Big, crushing, small.
sentences.zh: 宏大、压碎、渺小。

sentences.en: That story always seems to play itself out wherever there's a massive development.
sentences.zh: 无论哪里有大规模开发，那个故事似乎总是在重演。

sentences.en: But there's a theory that big buildings don't just hurt little people.
sentences.zh: 但有一种理论认为，大型建筑不仅伤害小人物。

sentences.en: They may, in fact, hurt the builders of those buildings, too.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们可能也会伤害这些建筑的建造者。

sentences.en: There is the well-known fact in real estate
sentences.zh: 房地产界有一个众所周知的事实，

sentences.en: that the great buildings tend to go up at the end of the cycle
sentences.zh: 即伟大的建筑往往在周期末期拔地而起，

sentences.en: when everything is about to turn.
sentences.zh: 当一切即将发生转折时。

sentences.en: That's the critic and philosopher Edward Tenor.
sentences.zh: 那是评论家兼哲学家爱德华·特诺尔说的。

sentences.en: While I was in Russia this last time,
sentences.zh: 我上次在俄罗斯的时候，

sentences.en: I found an essay online that he wrote in 2001,
sentences.zh: 在网上发现了他2001年写的一篇文章，

sentences.en: The Xanadu Effect.
sentences.zh: 《世外桃源效应》。

sentences.en: The Xanadu Effect is what I call the appearance of the big building,
sentences.zh: 我把大型建筑、大型结构的出现称为“世外桃源效应”，

sentences.en: the big structure, at the time when things are starting to go south.
sentences.zh: 即当事物开始走下坡路时出现的现象。

sentences.en: Tenor cites this idea known as the skyscraper curse,
sentences.zh: 特诺尔引用了一个被称为“摩天大楼诅咒”的观点，

sentences.en: that tall buildings correlate with bad times.
sentences.zh: 即高层建筑与糟糕的时期相关联。

sentences.en: So, for instance, the Empire State Building was conceived in the 1920s,
sentences.zh: 例如，帝国大厦是在20世纪20年代构思的，

sentences.en: but not finished until the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 但直到大萧条时期才完工。

sentences.en: When it was known as the empty state building.
sentences.zh: 当时它被称为“空置大厦”。

sentences.en: The Sears Tower and the World Trade Center both opened in 1973
sentences.zh: 西尔斯大厦和世界贸易中心都在1973年开业，

sentences.en: on the verge of another economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 正处于另一场经济危机的边缘。

sentences.en: The people who run the NASDAQ exchange
sentences.zh: 纳斯达克交易所的经营者们，

sentences.en: built the world's largest video display on Times Square in 1999,
sentences.zh: 在1999年于时代广场建造了世界上最大的视频显示屏，

sentences.en: just a few months before the dot-com bubble burst and the NASDAQ crashed.
sentences.zh: 就在互联网泡沫破裂和纳斯达克崩盘的前几个月。

sentences.en: The Xanadu Effect is a symptom of people overreaching, overplanning,
sentences.zh: “世外桃源效应”是人们过度扩张、过度规划的症状，

sentences.en: thinking that everything's going to go on forever
sentences.zh: 认为一切都会永远持续下去，

sentences.en: when it's about to turn the other way.
sentences.zh: 而实际上它即将走向反面。

sentences.en: I found Tenor's theory a little comforting.
sentences.zh: 我发现特诺尔的理论有点令人欣慰。

sentences.en: Plus, I think Olivia Newton-John's Xanadu is one of the biggest songs ever written.
sentences.zh: 另外，我认为奥莉维亚·纽顿-约翰的《世外桃源》是有史以来最伟大的歌曲之一。

sentences.en: I see what you're trying to do there, Julia, and it's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 我明白你想做什么，朱莉娅，但这行不通。

sentences.en: No Olivia Newton-John, but Coleridge, I will allow.
sentences.zh: 没有奥莉维亚·纽顿-约翰，但柯勒律治，我可以接受。

sentences.en: In Xanadu did Kubla Khan, a stately Pleasure Dome decree.
sentences.zh: 在世外桃源，忽必烈汗下令建造了一座庄严的享乐宫殿。

sentences.en: Actually, Tenor was thinking of the movie Citizen Kane and Kane's palace Xanadu.
sentences.zh: 事实上，特诺尔想到的是电影《公民凯恩》和凯恩的宫殿“世外桃源”。

sentences.en: Okay, then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: Rosebud.
sentences.zh: 玫瑰花蕾。

sentences.en: It was a sledge.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆雪橇。

sentences.en: So, just as Citizen Kane built his palace while his empire crumbled,
sentences.zh: 所以，正如公民凯恩在帝国崩溃时建造了他的宫殿一样，

sentences.en: the big project can be a big, bad distraction.
sentences.zh: 大型项目可能是一种巨大的、糟糕的干扰。

sentences.en: Tenor goes through several examples of the Xanadu Effect in his original essay,
sentences.zh: 特诺尔在他的原始文章中列举了几个“世外桃源效应”的例子，

sentences.en: but there are plenty of instances of big projects that don't pre-stage any kind of crash.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多大型项目并没有预示任何形式的崩溃。

sentences.en: Tenor cites the example of Cass Gilbert's Woolworth Building,
sentences.zh: 特诺尔引用了卡斯·吉尔伯特的伍尔沃斯大厦作为例子，

sentences.en: which went up in a boom time of 1913, and certainly didn't hurt the Woolworth Company.
sentences.zh: 它在1913年的繁荣时期建成，当然没有损害伍尔沃斯公司。

sentences.en: And it's hard to say where these gigantic state-driven projects like the Olympics fit into Xanadu.
sentences.zh: 而且很难说像奥运会这样由国家驱动的巨大项目如何归入“世外桃源”范畴。

sentences.en: Plus, there are plenty of critics who argue that building height, much less bigness in general,
sentences.zh: 此外，还有许多评论家认为，建筑高度，更不用说一般的宏大，

sentences.en: cannot accurately predict a downturn at all.
sentences.zh: 根本无法准确预测经济衰退。

sentences.en: Bigness is a strategy that just about always fails unless it succeeds.
sentences.zh: 宏大是一种几乎总是失败的策略，除非它成功了。

sentences.en: Or you could say it's one that always succeeds except when it fails.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以说，这是一种除了失败之外总是成功的策略。

sentences.en: And there's really no one way that you can regard it.
sentences.zh: 而且你真的无法用单一的方式来看待它。

sentences.en: You have to see it as a very powerful, easy-to-misuse,
sentences.zh: 你必须把它看作是一种非常强大、容易被滥用，

sentences.en: but also tempting way to go about things in life.
sentences.zh: 但同时也是生活中一种诱人的行事方式。

sentences.en: So the Xanadu Effect might not provide the comeuppance that Julia desires.
sentences.zh: 所以“世外桃源效应”可能并不能提供朱莉娅所渴望的那种报应。

sentences.en: Besides, in any sort of downturn, the little person is still the one most likely to suffer.
sentences.zh: 此外，在任何形式的衰退中，小人物仍然是最容易受苦的人。

sentences.en: I guess the success or failure of bigness really does depend on where you stand in relation to it.
sentences.zh: 我想宏大的成功或失败确实取决于你与它所处的位置。

sentences.en: Are you on top of City Hall or down below?
sentences.zh: 你是站在市政厅顶上，还是在下面？

sentences.en: Big places just amplify our reactions.
sentences.zh: 宏大的地方只会放大我们的反应。

sentences.en: I went to a protest in Moscow where we marched down one of the city's wide Soviet-era boulevards.
sentences.zh: 我参加了莫斯科的一次抗议活动，我们沿着城市中一条宽阔的苏联时代大道游行。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, I hate these boulevards because you can't actually cross them.
sentences.zh: 通常，我讨厌这些大道，因为你根本无法穿过它们。

sentences.en: You have to find a pedestrian tunnel and, like, sneak underneath.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到一条人行隧道，像那样偷偷穿过去。

sentences.en: But for a few hours, Moscow's oppressive bigness became ours.
sentences.zh: 但有几个小时，莫斯科那种压抑的宏大变成了我们的。

sentences.en: The wide road, those Stalin-era skyscrapers and block-long institutes,
sentences.zh: 宽阔的道路、那些斯大林时代的摩天大楼和长达一个街区的机构，

sentences.en: it all made us feel bigger, too, though it was freezing.
sentences.zh: 这一切也让我们感觉自己更宏大了，尽管当时天气很冷。

sentences.en: I love that despite the cold, people are smiling.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尽管天气寒冷，人们依然在微笑。

sentences.en: Everybody is.
sentences.zh: 每个人都是。

sentences.en: That's my friend Vasily Sonkin.
sentences.zh: 那是我的朋友瓦西里·桑金。

sentences.en: He grew up in Moscow, but he'd never experienced his grandiose city like this
sentences.zh: 他在莫斯科长大，但他从未像这样体验过他那宏大的城市，

sentences.en: as a grandiose stage for political expression.
sentences.zh: 作为政治表达的宏大舞台。

sentences.en: The way the crowds transformed the National Mall in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 就像人群改变华盛顿特区的国家广场，

sentences.en: or the Champs-Élysées in Paris.
sentences.zh: 或是巴黎的香榭丽舍大街那样。

sentences.en: And even Edward Tenor says that's what can be wonderful about bigness.
sentences.zh: 甚至连爱德华·特诺尔也说，这就是宏大可能带来的美妙之处。

sentences.en: It can elevate people, give them a sense of pride and purpose.
sentences.zh: 它可以提升人们，给他们一种自豪感和目标感。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the positive side of our cities are the big buildings when they're done well.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们城市积极的一面很大程度上在于那些建造得很好的大型建筑。

sentences.en: New York without the Empire State Building, New York without the Chrysler Building,
sentences.zh: 没有帝国大厦的纽约，没有克莱斯勒大厦的纽约，

sentences.en: New York without Rockefeller Center would really be a poorer place.
sentences.zh: 没有洛克菲勒中心的纽约，真的会是一个更贫乏的地方。

sentences.en: But I keep thinking about Alexei Kravitz and his standoff with developers in Sochi.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在想阿列克谢·克拉维茨和他与索契开发商的对峙。

sentences.en: Sometimes he goes out and films his confrontations with construction workers.
sentences.zh: 有时他会出去拍摄他与建筑工人的冲突。

sentences.en: I posted one of the films up on 99percentinvisible.org.
sentences.zh: 我把其中一段视频发布在了 99percentinvisible.org 上。

sentences.en: Everyone's speaking Russian, but it's not hard to understand what is going on.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说俄语，但不难理解发生了什么。

sentences.en: Kravitz had put some of his things in a metal storage unit behind his house.
sentences.zh: 克拉维茨把他的一些东西放在了房子后面的一个金属储物柜里。

sentences.en: The workers showed up with a huge crane to haul it away.
sentences.zh: 工人们带着一台巨大的起重机出现，要把东西拖走。

sentences.en: Kravitz asks who they work for.
sentences.zh: 克拉维茨问他们为谁工作。

sentences.en: And the supervisor, this big burly guy, says,
sentences.zh: 而那个主管，那个身材魁梧的家伙说，

sentences.en: We are building the Olympic facilities.
sentences.zh: 我们正在建设奥运设施。

sentences.en: Then they hook up the crane while Kravitz shouts at them.
sentences.zh: 然后他们挂上起重机，克拉维茨对着他们大喊大叫。

sentences.en: You can see a big building under construction behind them.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他们身后有一座正在建设中的大型建筑。

sentences.en: That's a new train station which will take in millions of visitors during the Olympic Games.
sentences.zh: 那是一个新的火车站，在奥运会期间将接待数百万游客。

sentences.en: You can see the bones of what's going to be a soaring roof.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到未来将成为高耸屋顶的骨架。

sentences.en: A stately pleasure dome.
sentences.zh: 一座庄严的享乐宫殿。

sentences.en: A stately pleasure dome.
sentences.zh: 一座庄严的享乐宫殿。

sentences.en: Julia Barton traveled most recently to Russia for PRI's The World.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅·巴顿最近为 PRI 的《世界》节目前往俄罗斯。

sentences.en: You can find more of her stories at JuliaBarton.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 JuliaBarton.com 找到她更多的报道。

sentences.en: 99 Percent Invisible was produced this week by Julia Barton with a little help from me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由朱莉娅·巴顿制作，并得到了我，罗曼·马尔斯的少许帮助。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山 KALW 91.7 本地公共广播电台的一个项目。

sentences.en: and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 以及旧金山的美国建筑师协会。

sentences.en: Support for 99 Percent Invisible is provided in part by tiny letter.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》的部分赞助由 Tiny Letter 提供。

sentences.en: Email for people with something to say.
sentences.zh: 专为有话要说的人打造的电子邮件服务。

sentences.en: My boy Carver always has something to say.
sentences.zh: 我的儿子卡弗总是有话要说。

sentences.en: What do you have to say, Carver?
sentences.zh: 卡弗，你想说什么？

sentences.en: Daddy, long legals.
sentences.zh: 爸爸，盲蛛。

sentences.en: They have eight legs to six feet up to 10 and that's right.
sentences.zh: 它们有八条腿，六只脚，甚至多达十只，没错。

sentences.en: They are arachnids, but they are not spiders.
sentences.zh: 它们属于蛛形纲，但并不是蜘蛛。

sentences.en: That's a load off my mind.
sentences.zh: 这下我放心了。

sentences.en: It's free, easy, minimal, powerful, the simplest way to write an email newsletter.
sentences.zh: 它免费、简单、极简、强大，是撰写电子邮件通讯最简单的方式。

sentences.en: Online at tinyletter.com.
sentences.zh: 网址是 tinyletter.com。

sentences.en: This program is distributed by PRX, the public radio exchange,
sentences.zh: 本节目由公共广播交流平台 PRX 发行，

sentences.en: making public radio more public.
sentences.zh: 旨在让公共广播更加大众化。

sentences.en: More at prx.org.
sentences.zh: 更多信息请访问 prx.org。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注本节目。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: You can always just catch up with us online at 99percentinvisible.org.
sentences.zh: 你也可以随时访问 99percentinvisible.org 在线收听。

sentences.en: Hello to Jason Isaacs.
sentences.zh: 向杰森·艾萨克问好。
